blocks.text: Al-Kabeer The Most Great means the One who has al-kibriyaa' greatness (majesty/pride) as a description and al-'adhamah might as an attribute.
In a hadeeth qudsee on the authority of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
Allaah said: "Pride is my cloak and greatness my robe, and he who competes with Me in respect of either of them I shall cast into Hell-fire".
blocks.ref: Musnad Imaam Ahmad 2/248; Sunan Aboo Daawood 4090

blocks.text: Allaah has these two descriptions of majesty and might and their value cannot be comprehended nor can they be grasped in their entirety.

If a Muslim believes and has faith that Allaah is greater than everything and that no matter how great something may be it will be insignificant to Allaah's greatness and might. He will humble himself to his Lord and submit in front of Him. He will perform different types of worship for Him and he will believe that Allaah deserves this worship and no one else does. He will know that every polytheist will not give His Great Lord the due he deserves. As Allaah said,

They made not a just estimate of Allah such as is due to Him. And on the Day of Resurrection the whole of the earth will be grasped by His Hand and the heavens will be rolled up in His Right Hand. Glorified is He, and High is He above all that they associate as partners with Him!

Allaah is far removed from every imperfection, subhaanAllaah. Where have the intellects of the polytheists gone when they direct their humility and humbleness to lowly creation and ignoble created beings that do not possess anything of benefit or harm for themselves never mind possessing them for others. They left humbleness and humility of the Mighty Lord, the Great, the Exalted, the Majestic Creator to whom faces are humbled, voices are hushed, hearts tremble out of awe and heads lowered. Blessed be Allaah the Lord of the worlds.

keyPoints: Al-Kabeer means the One who has greatness (al-kibriyaa': majesty/pride) as a description and might (al-'adhamah) as an attribute.
In a hadeeth qudsee Allaah said: "Pride is my cloak and greatness my robe", and whoever competes with Him in either will be cast into Hell-fire.
The value of these two descriptions of majesty and might cannot be comprehended nor grasped in their entirety.
Whoever believes Allaah is greater than everything humbles himself to his Lord and believes that only He deserves worship.
The polytheists did not make a just estimate of Allaah, directing their humility to lowly creation that possesses no benefit or harm.

recall.a: The One who has greatness (majesty/pride, al-kibriyaa') as a description and might (al-'adhamah) as an attribute.

recall.q: What does the hadeeth qudsee say about pride and greatness?
recall.a: "Pride is my cloak and greatness my robe, and he who competes with Me in respect of either of them I shall cast into Hell-fire."

recall.q: What is the effect on a Muslim who believes Allaah is greater than everything?
recall.a: He humbles himself to his Lord, submits to Him, performs worship for Him and believes that only Allaah deserves this worship.

recall.q: Which aayah does the author cite to show the polytheists did not give Allaah His due?
recall.a: Zumar 39:67: 'They made not a just estimate of Allah such as is due to Him...'

recall.q: What is the meaning of Al-'Adheem, and what does the book say about the descriptions of majesty and might?
recall.a: Al-'Adheem means The Magnificent. Allaah has the two descriptions of majesty (al-kibriyaa') and might (al-'adhamah), and their value cannot be comprehended nor grasped in their entirety.
